resources.string: DNS to a remote resolver over Shadowsocks
Remote DNS target on the SS server
Adds IPv6 DNS and routing to the VPN. Disable if your server or network has no IPv6. Applies after a VPN restart.
Only the system resolver goes to the remote DNS. All other traffic uses the native network path. Hardcoded plain DNS bypasses.
Every TCP/UDP port-53 query goes to the remote DNS. All other traffic stays direct through a userspace forwarder.
All app traffic goes through Shadowsocks. DNS still goes to the remote DNS over SS. Slowest mode.
Grant VPN permission by pressing Start once.
Quick Settings tiles are not supported on this device; add it manually.
Could not add the tile. Add it manually in Quick Settings.
Private DNS uses port 853 and can bypass dns2ss. Turn it off while using dns2ss.
DoH (port 443) can bypass dns2ss. Disable browser secure DNS and block DoH hostnames in the remote DNS blocklist.
Network changes automatically restart the VPN. If DNS still fails after switching networks, stop and start once.
Logging changes apply after the VPN is restarted.
dns2ss is fail-closed: if the SS tunnel or remote DNS is unavailable, DNS fails instead of leaking to the local resolver.
